title: Non-HTTP Primitives: SMB and LDAP as exec_plan Steps
goal: Extend the exec_plan grammar to allow SMB (list shares, file read, NTLM auth attempt) and LDAP (bind, search) as step types alongside HTTP. This is the first move toward truly universal cross-protocol attack composition: AI can now write a single exec_plan that proves web -> SMB or web -> LDAP chains in one continuous narrative.
scope: Extend workers/runners/exec_plan/runner.py with two new step kinds: smb_request (subcommands list/read/auth using existing impacket or netexec primitives) and ldap_request (using existing ldap_enum primitives). Reuse the existing scope check + capture/expect/on_success contract. Schema updates documented in system prompt minimally.
generation_reason: exec_plan currently composes HTTP only. Cross-target chains demand non-HTTP step types. SMB and LDAP are the two highest-value additions because they unlock the canonical web -> infra -> AD pivot story. Underlying tooling (impacket, netexec, ldap_enum) already exists as runners; this exposes them as primitives Claude can compose.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: SMB + LDAP only. Do NOT add SSH, RDP, Kerberos, or DNS step kinds in this task. Those are follow-up scope.
constraints.reuse_existing: Implementation MUST wrap existing impacket/netexec/ldap_enum primitives, not re-implement protocol clients.
constraints.scope_governance: SMB step kinds are intrusive tier by default. LDAP queries can be active tier (read-only).
constraints.system_prompt_minimal: System prompt grammar section gets a brief addendum showing the two new step kinds. Do NOT rewrite existing exec_plan grammar.

success_criteria: exec_plan accepts step kind smb_request with at least list_shares, read_file, ntlm_auth_attempt subcommands.
exec_plan accepts step kind ldap_request with bind + search subcommands.
Each new step kind respects scope_allowlist (host check) and intrusive-tier gating.
Capture/expect contract works on the new step kinds (e.g. capture domain controller hostname from LDAP search, expect specific ACE).
Unit tests cover happy path + scope rejection for each new step kind.
Live integration test on a lab AD environment proves at least one web -> ldap chain via a single exec_plan.

acceptance_criteria: exec_plan can compose at least one HTTP + LDAP step in a single plan and emit a finding from the chain.
Scope and tier checks block out-of-scope or improperly-tiered SMB/LDAP steps.
No regression in existing exec_plan HTTP step tests.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the single active task.
backlog-384 and backlog-385 must be merged.

out_of_scope: Full AD pack with BloodHound chain reasoning (would be next-phase work).
